issues.legal_issue: A co-owner may institute eviction proceedings against a tenant without proving the consent of the other co-owners, unless another co-owner objects.
material_facts: The landlord owned the shop jointly with his four sisters.
He sought eviction of the tenant for his own bona fide business requirement.
There was no evidence that any of his sisters objected to the eviction proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The eviction proceeding was maintainable even though the landlord had not shown that his sisters had consented to it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13 of the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, an eviction proceeding may be brought by a co-owner. Applying the doctrine of agency, one co-owner acts on his own behalf and as agent for the others; their consent is presumed unless it is shown that they objected. The Court relied on India Umbrella Manufacturing Co. v. Bhagabandei Agarwalla, which in turn referred to Sri Ram Pasricha v. Jagannath and Dhannalal v. Kalawatibai.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and applicant_is_co_owner and not other_co_owner_objected

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding is one brought by a landlord to evict a tenant from rented property.
predicates.applicant_is_co_owner: The person bringing the proceeding owns the property jointly with one or more other people.
predicates.other_co_owner_objected: Another co-owner opposed the eviction proceeding.

issues.definition: When a co-owner brings a tenant-eviction proceeding and no other co-owner objects, the co-owner may seek eviction.

issues.legal_issue: Lack of experience in a proposed business does not by itself prevent a landlord from establishing a bona fide personal requirement for rented premises.
material_facts: The landlord sought the shop to run a wholesale business in Ayurvedic medicines after retiring from employment.
The appellate authority found that his personal requirement was bona fide, and the High Court affirmed that finding.
No statutory qualification or experience requirement applied to running the proposed business.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was not required to prove prior experience in the proposed business as a precondition to seeking eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, provided the basis for seeking eviction on the asserted personal requirement. The Court held that business experience is not a precondition unless a statute prescribes a qualification or other requirement for starting the business; it noted that no such requirement applied to the proposed wholesale Ayurvedic-medicine business.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding is one brought by a landlord to evict a tenant from rented property.
predicates.bona_fide_personal_requirement_proved: The landlord has established that the premises are genuinely required for the landlord's own use.
predicates.business_has_no_legal_experience_require: No applicable law makes prior experience a requirement for starting the landlord's proposed business.

issues.definition: In a tenant-eviction proceeding, a landlord who proves a genuine personal requirement is not barred from eviction merely for lacking business experience when no law requires such experience.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings that a landlord has a bona fide personal requirement should not be disturbed without an appropriate basis for doing so.
material_facts: The appellate authority found that the landlord had a bona fide requirement for the shop.
The High Court affirmed that finding after considering the matter from all aspects.
The Supreme Court found no appropriate basis to disturb the factual finding.
issues.conclusion: The finding of bona fide personal requirement was left undisturbed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that it should not disturb a factual finding of bona fide requirement reached by the appellate authority and affirmed by the High Court unless an appropriate case is made out.

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_finding: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a finding made in a tenant-eviction case.
predicates.lower_courts_concurrently_found_bona_fid: The appellate court and the High Court both found that the landlord genuinely required the premises for personal use.
predicates.appropriate_basis_to_disturb_finding: There is a proper basis for the reviewing court to set aside the concurrent factual finding.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a concurrent finding of genuine personal requirement in an eviction case and there is no proper basis to set it aside, the finding remains undisturbed.
